 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the M.V.Act'), calling in question the Judgment and award dated 13.04.2018 passed in MVC No.845/2017 on the file of the VIII Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge, &
Addl. MACT, Belagavi (hereinafter referred to as 'the tribunal').
Smt. Renuka W/O Tukaram Belagoji vs Shri. Mallanagouda S/O Shivangouda ...

The brief facts of the case are that, on 29.11.2016 at about 23.00 hours the deceased Shankar Vasudev Chougule and Somanath Belagoji and others, were returning back to Santi Bastwad after taking Darshan, on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-22/ET-9956 with moderate speed on the left side of the road and when they reached the spot near Peeranwadi-Jamboti road, near Renakunde cross,
Santi-Bastwad, Belgavi, one Bolero Goods (LGV) Jeep bearing registration No.KA-28/B-5979 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came in a rash and negligent manner and the driver of the same lost control over it and went to wrong side from the opposite direction and caused accident by dashing to the motorcycle.
Due to the said accident, the riders of the motorcycle i.e. Shankar Vasudev Chougule and Somanath Tukaram Belagoji, both were died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Thereafter, the legal heirs of the deceased i.e. claimants/appellants in the present appellant have filed claim petition in MVC No.845/2017 claiming compensation.

3. The tribunal after appreciating the materials on record and the evidence placed before it, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.8,11,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The tribunal held respondent No.2 therein i.e. Insurance company liable to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the said award, the claimants/appellants have preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal.

4. We have heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance company and perused the materials on record, including the trial Court records.

5. The compensation awarded by the tribunal under different heads are as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Rs.7,56,000/-
2. Loss of love and affection Rs.25,000/-
3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4. Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.8,11,000/-
6.

As could be seen from the order of the tribunal, the tribunal has taken into consideration the income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/-, which is on lower side and as per the Lok Adalath chart, the tribunal ought to have taken the income of the deceased as Rs.8,750/- per month.
Admittedly, the deceased is aged about 22 years.
The tribunal has also taken the age of the deceased as 22 years.

Hence, future prospectus should be 40% and the appropriate multiplier would be '18'
and the deceased is since a bachelor 50% should be deducted from the income.

Hence, Rs.3,500/-
(40% future prospectus) + Rs.8,750/- (Notional income as per the Lok Adalath Chart)

3 minus 50% (since bachelor) = Rs.6,125/-.

Therefore, the loss of dependency would be Rs.6,125/-
X18X12 = Rs.13,23,000/-.

Since there are two dependents i.e. mother and brother, Rs.40,000/-
each under the head of consortium, which comes to Rs.80,000/-.
The tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Hence, the claimants are entitle for compensation as under:
1. Loss of annual dependency Rs.13,23,000/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-
3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4. Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Total Rs.14,33,000/-
 Compensation awarded by the trial Rs.8,11,000/-
 Court  Compensation enhanced by this Court Rs.6,22,000/-
7.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitle for additional compensation of Rs.6,22,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal.
